assumptions.status: Hypothetical iris assumptions; only the colorimetry tables and the eumelanin wavelength exponent are sourced

colorimetry.colour_space: CIE 1976 L*a*b*; white is a perfect reflector under the same sampled tables

measured_anchors.source: van den Berg, IJspeert and de Waard 1991, Vision Research 31:1361-1367, PMID 1891824; abstract read, full text not
measured_anchors.claim: For a light-blue eye effective transmission of the iris was 1% for red and 0.2% for green light
measured_anchors.limits: Non-albino iris. Transmission through the whole iris, not a round-trip return. The abstract reports dark-brown eyes two orders of magnitude lower. No albinism value was found.

eumelanin_spectral_exponent.source: Jacques, https://omlc.org/spectra/melanin/mua.html (page copyright 1998 Steven Jacques; retrieved 2026-10-26; page sha256 0189e5bfd62a258bace15270d5e65615c1a6ee7093583766b308d8b40cd96d56). The page gives mu_a = 1.70e12 nm^-3.48 cm^-1 for skin and 6.49e12 nm^-3.48 cm^-1 for retina melanosome interiors and says ten-fold variation is to be expected. Only the exponent is used. It cites Jacques and McAuliffe 1991 (PMID 1886936; abstract read, full text not) and Jacques et al. 1996.
eumelanin_spectral_exponent.limits: Skin and retinal melanosomes, not iris, and not pheomelanin. The absolute magnitude is not used.

pheomelanin_spectral_exponent.status: assumed and swept; no visible-range measurement found in open sources
pheomelanin_spectral_exponent.qualitative_support: Peles and Simon 2010 (PMID 20614877; abstract read) report pheomelanin absorption 1.2 times eumelanin at 244 nm and infer it is lower at 315-400 nm, so it may fall off faster. That is ultraviolet only.

stroma_backscatter.status: assumed and swept, then calibrated: only settings whose pigment-free stroma over a dark back falls in the blue window are used for interpretation
stroma_backscatter.note: No quantitative open source for iris stroma scattering amplitude or wavelength dependence was found. A Monte Carlo model of lightly pigmented irides exists (Baranoski and Lam 2007, DOI 10.1117/1.2747205); its title resolved and it was not read.

back_return_modes.status: assumed and swept; the red edge position and width are assumed; see measured_anchors for the only related measurement found

notes: Absorbance values are single-pass over the stroma at 550 nm for the combined melanins.
The pheomelanin exponent is the assumption that lets pheomelanin shift hue; 25 is a near-step edge chosen to test an extreme.
Backscatter is bounded (fraction at 550 nm times (550/lambda)^exponent, capped at 1).
The translucent_red_return modes stand in for a reddish return through a pigment-poor, translucent iris.
A case is classified only if its luminance Y is at least the stated fraction of the reference's, so very dark pigment-saturated cases are not counted as orange or purple.
Colour uses the CIE tables in cie-tables/, sampled at the model wavelengths. CIELAB hue angle does not change when a spectrum is uniformly dimmed, so brightness and hue are judged separately.
D65 is a reference daylight, not a viewing condition. Real appearance also depends on lighting, adaptation, surroundings and camera processing.
Windows are hue-angle ranges centred on reference spectra chosen for this exploration; they are not definitions of the words orange or purple.
